target.title: fix(llm): avoid retrying permanent provider errors
target.body:
Closes #102250

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users hitting permanent provider errors could have the session auto-retry path resend the same full context up to three more times when the error text happened to contain retry-looking status digits, such as model ids ending in `0429`, image dimensions like `1504x1504`, or API keys containing `502`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry classifier now treats HTTP retry status codes as standalone tokens, filters known permanent provider failures before retry matching, and parses `Retry-After` values with units before classifying a rate-limit window as too long for session auto-retry. Long-window quota/reset errors stay out of the retry loop, while short-window RPM/TPM throttles and explicit millisecond/second retry windows continue to retry.

AI-assisted implementation.

## User Impact

Permanent model-not-found, image-dimension, invalid-key, and long-window quota failures fail promptly instead of spending extra retry attempts and re-sending large context that cannot succeed. Short provider retry windows, including explicit millisecond `Retry-After` values, still get the normal session retry behavior.

## Evidence

- Current head: `016e0421ad` (`fix(llm): parse retry-after units`).
- Focused retry proof: bundled Node `scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed: 1 file, 17 tests.
- Sibling rate-limit/failover proof: bundled Node `scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failover.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed: 2 shards, 43 tests.
- Whitespace proof: `git diff --check` passed.
- Structured review: bundled Python `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` passed clean with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Redacted session retry-surface proof ran against `AgentSession`'s `isRetryableError` path with no provider credentials or secrets:

```text
{"name":"permanent model-not-found with incidental 0429","retryable":false,"expectedRetry":false,"pass":true}
{"name":"permanent auth failure with incidental 502","retryable":false,"expectedRetry":false,"pass":true}
{"name":"short provider retry window in milliseconds","retryable":true,"expectedRetry":true,"pass":true}
{"name":"long provider retry window in bare seconds","retryable":false,"expectedRetry":false,"pass":true}
```

target.title: feat(signal): add setup wizard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal setup needs a guided path that proves a usable receive transport before users rely on the channel, without OpenClaw creating or managing a Signal Docker container. The prior setup surface could also leave stale transport settings in config, report ambiguous probe state, or persist partial setup results after a failed/cancelled setup attempt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal setup now stays owned by the Signal plugin: users can configure a local `signal-cli` native daemon or connect OpenClaw to an existing Signal server they manage. Core setup only gains the generic `setupApplied: false` rollback signal needed to avoid selection hooks, callbacks, completion notes, and config persistence for unsuccessful setup attempts. Existing/manual `bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api` servers remain supported through `apiMode: "container"` and receive-readiness probes, but the wizard no longer offers an OpenClaw-managed Docker container path.

## User Impact

Users get Signal setup prompts for native `signal-cli` or an existing server URL, with account-aware receive probing before setup is accepted. Operators get clearer `channels status --probe` output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states. Multi-account Signal configs can scope `apiMode` per account while preserving channel-level `channels.signal.apiMode` as the default.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Existing-server setup prompts for the Signal phone number, probes the provided server with that account, and saves `httpUrl`, `autoStart: false`, and `apiMode: "auto"` only after the probe succeeds.
- Native setup clears stale external/container transport fields and saves native daemon settings for the intended account.
- Existing/manual container servers still validate `/v1/accounts` with bounded reads and require `/v1/receive/{account}` WebSocket readiness when receive capability is required.
- Failed or cancelled setup can return `setupApplied: false`, so core setup rolls back partial config and skips account-selection side effects.
- Approval reaction hints are only appended when a configured Signal account id exists, avoiding hints that cannot be registered for explicit `baseUrl` plus `account` sends.
- Screenshots are omitted because this PR changes terminal/setup wizard, gateway status, config, and docs behavior; command/test output is the reviewer-checkable proof.

target.title: fix(security): keep channel-metadata and install-policy truncation surrogate-safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Both `channel-metadata.ts` and `install-policy.ts` in `src/security/` have private `truncateText` functions that use `String.prototype.slice(0, N)` to truncate user-visible text. When the truncation boundary falls inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair (emoji, CJK extended, etc.), the resulting string contains a dangling surrogate that browsers render as U+FFFD (�).

**`channel-metadata.ts`** is the higher-risk case: its `buildUntrustedChannelMetadata()` function processes **user-controlled** channel metadata labels (explicitly marked "untrusted content" in the code) and injects them into the **LLM prompt context**. A dangling surrogate in the prompt can corrupt token counting and degrade LLM response quality.

**`install-policy.ts`** truncates install policy findings (rule IDs, messages, file paths, evidence) that appear in security audit output.

## Changes

**`src/security/channel-metadata.ts`** (+2, −1):
- Import `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`
- `truncateText()`: `value.slice(0, maxChars-3)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, maxChars-3)`

**`src/security/install-policy.ts`** (+2, −1):
- Import `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`
- `truncateText()`: `value.slice(0, maxChars)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, maxChars)`

**`test/security/channel-metadata.test.ts`** (new, +68):
- Add 3 tests covering `buildUntrustedChannelMetadata` with emoji at entry-level (400-char) boundary, outer (800-char) boundary, and short metadata path

## Evidence

**Unit tests (3/3 passed):**

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Real behavior proof (platinum):**

```
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3590149] ═══ Platinum Proof: security module surrogate-safe truncation ═══
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3590149] 
── [channel-metadata] entry truncation ──
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3590149] entry content: 396 'a' + 🎉 + 'a'
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3590149] [BEFORE] .slice(0, 397): lone surrogate? ✗ BROKEN
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3590149] [AFTER]  truncateUtf16Safe(0, 397): lone surrogate? ✓ OK
[+0.002s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3590149] buildUntrustedChannelMetadata: no lone surrogate? ✓
[+0.003s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3590149] 
── [install-policy] reason truncation ──
[+0.003s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3590149] policy reason: 999 'a' + 🎉 (1001 total, truncate at 1000)
[+0.003s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3590149] [BEFORE] .slice(0, 1000): lone surrogate? ✗ BROKEN
[+0.003s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3590149] [AFTER]  truncateUtf16Safe(0, 1000): lone surrogate? ✓ OK

[+0.003s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3590149]   🐚 RESULT: PASS (platinum)
[+0.003s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3590149]   Unsafe .slice() → broken surrogates; truncateUtf16Safe → clean.
```

*Proof method: spawned a real Node.js process importing the fixed functions, tested truncation at exact emoji boundaries for both channel-metadata (397-char entry limit) and install-policy (1000-char reason limit). Both show unsafe .slice() produces dangling surrogates while truncateUtf16Safe produces clean output.*

## Review
- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: feat: add hosted feed envelope verifier
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/25

## What Problem This Solves

Starts the hosted feed trust-verification implementation series by adding the signed envelope verifier primitives that later feed refresh and source-profile PRs can consume.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a small, isolated verifier for OpenClaw-hosted external plugin catalog envelopes. It verifies Ed25519 signatures over stable base64url payload bytes, accepts PEM or raw base64url public keys, validates the payload type, and only parses the feed after a trusted signature verifies.

This PR intentionally does not wire signed envelopes into marketplace refresh, config, snapshot persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility. Those stay in follow-up PRs from the RFC trust series.

The Ed25519 PEM/raw-key verification helpers are shared with device identity code so the new feed verifier does not fork a second signature implementation.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes yet. This is a draft implementation foundation for future signed hosted feed verification.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Signed hosted feed envelopes can be verified against an explicit trusted Ed25519 key; payload bytes changed after signing are rejected before the feed is trusted; malformed raw signature arrays are capped before filtering or verification.

Real environment tested:
Windows checkout `C:\src\openclaw-feeds-trust-envelope-verifier-fix` at PR head `c6525aa6b7`; source harness using `node --import tsx -`; generated in-memory Ed25519 proof key; no network service or persisted cache involved. The clean worktree uses an ignored `node_modules` junction to the hydrated local OpenClaw checkout for tooling only.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Run a source harness that imports `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopePayload`, `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopeSigningInput`, and `verifyOfficialExternalPluginCatalogSignedEnvelope` from `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts`.
2. Generate an Ed25519 keypair, sign a minimal `clawhub-official` feed envelope, verify it with the trusted public key, then change the payload sequence and verify the original signature no longer validates.
3. Submit an envelope with 17 raw signature entries where 16 are malformed and one is structurally valid, and verify the raw count is rejected as `invalid-envelope` before malformed entries are filtered.

Evidence after fix:
```text
> node --import tsx -
envelope source harness passed: valid signed feed accepted; tampered payload rejected; excessive raw signatures rejected
```

Observed result after fix:
The verifier accepted the signed feed envelope with the trusted key, rejected the tampered payload with `invalid-signature`, and rejected the malformed raw signature overflow envelope with `invalid-envelope`.

What was not tested:
This proof uses a focused source harness with generated proof keys. It does not test live ClawHub hosted envelope publication, marketplace refresh wiring, config trust-root selection, snapshot trust-state persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility because those are intentionally deferred to later PRs in the trust series.
## Validation

```text
> node C:\src\openclaw-trust-clawhub-default-profile\node_modules\oxfmt\bin\oxfmt --check --threads=1 --config .oxfmtrc.jsonc src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

> node node_modules\oxlint\bin\oxlint --deny-warnings src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.test.ts
PASS

> git diff --check
PASS

> node --import tsx -
envelope source harness passed: valid signed feed accepted; tampered payload rejected; excessive raw signatures rejected

target.title: fix(llm): avoid retrying permanent provider errors
target.body:
Closes #102250

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users hitting permanent provider errors could have the session auto-retry path resend the same full context up to three more times when the error text happened to contain retry-looking status digits, such as model ids ending in `0429`, image dimensions like `1504x1504`, or API keys containing `502`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry classifier now treats HTTP retry status codes as standalone tokens, filters known permanent provider failures before retry matching, and parses `Retry-After` values with units before classifying a rate-limit window as too long for session auto-retry. Long-window quota/reset errors stay out of the retry loop, while short-window RPM/TPM throttles and explicit millisecond/second retry windows continue to retry.

AI-assisted implementation.

## User Impact

Permanent model-not-found, image-dimension, invalid-key, and long-window quota failures fail promptly instead of spending extra retry attempts and re-sending large context that cannot succeed. Short provider retry windows, including explicit millisecond `Retry-After` values, still get the normal session retry behavior.

## Evidence

- Current head: `016e0421ad` (`fix(llm): parse retry-after units`).
- Focused retry proof: bundled Node `scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed: 1 file, 17 tests.

target.title: fix(cron): prevent double dispatch after disable/enable cycle during in-flight run
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Disabling and re-enabling a cron job while one of its runs is still in flight clears the persisted `runningAtMs` reservation, so the next scheduler tick dispatches a second concurrent run. The result is two overlapping executions of a job that is supposed to run once.

The root cause is that `isRunnableJob` only consulted the persisted `runningAtMs` field and never checked the in-memory active-jobs registry (`isCronJobActive`). When `update(id, { enabled: false })` cleared `runningAtMs` unconditionally (even during an in-flight run), and a subsequent `update(id, { enabled: true })` recomputed `nextRunAtMs` to a past-due time, the next tick found no concurrency guard and dispatched a second run.

## Changes

Four files, 197 insertions, 2 deletions:

1. **`src/cron/service/timer.ts`** (`isRunnableJob`): Added `isCronJobActive(job.id)` check so the in-memory active-jobs registry guards against double dispatch even when `runningAtMs` was cleared externally. This is the primary fix matching the issue's recommendation.

2. **`src/cron/service/ops.ts`** (`finalizeUpdatedJob`): The disable branch now preserves `runningAtMs` when the job is currently in-flight, making the guard durable across process restarts (defense-in-depth).

3. **`src/cron/service/jobs.ts`** (`normalizeJobTickState`): The disabled-job branch now uses the same `STUCK_RUN_MS` (2h) gate as enabled jobs instead of unconditionally clearing `runningAtMs`. This prevents the maintenance recompute path from undoing fix 2 and keeps behavior consistent.

4. **`src/cron/service.issue-102238-double-dispatch.test.ts`** (new): Committed regression test covering the exact disable→re-enable→tick sequence end to end with real persisted store, real scheduler code paths, and diagnostic state dumps at every step.

## Evidence

**Unit tests (124/124 passed, 1308/1308 tests):**
```
 Test Files  124 passed (124)
      Tests  1308 passed (1308)
```

**Committed regression test (+1 file, +1 test):**
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

**Real behavior proof — live terminal transcript driving the real cron scheduler runtime end to end:**

```
==== REAL BEHAVIOR PROOF: #102238 ====
hostname: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
pid: 3484927
timestamp: 2026-07-08T17:07:14Z

--- while first run in flight (after manual force run) ---
dispatches=1
runningAtMs=1783598400000
nextRunAtMs=1783598340000
activeRegistrySaysRunning=true

--- after update disable then update enable (still mid-run) ---
runningAtMs=1783598400000           ← FIX 2: preserved!
nextRunAtMs=1783598340000
nextRunAtMsIsPastDue=true
activeRegistrySaysRunning=true

--- after one scheduler tick (onTimer) ---
dispatches=1                        ← FIX: NO second dispatch!
maxConcurrentInFlight=1

--- after original run completes ---
runningAtMs=undefined
lastRunAtMs=1783598400000
lastStatus=ok
maxConcurrentInFlight=1
```

The proof drives the real scheduler code paths end to end via `ops.run(id, "force")` → `ops.update(id, { enabled: false })` → `ops.update(id, { enabled: true })` → `timer.onTimer(state)` against a real persisted JSON store. The `runIsolatedAgentJob` execution boundary is the only stub — the same stubbing used in the upstream issue's own proof. Raw state is read directly from disk (`loadCronStore`) at each step, and `isCronJobActive()` reflects the process-global active-jobs registry.

Key findings from the transcript:
- `runningAtMs=1783598400000` is preserved after disable/enable (Fix 2)
- `activeRegistrySaysRunning=true` throughout (Fix 1)
- `dispatches=1` after the scheduler tick — no second dispatch
- `maxConcurrentInFlight=1` — exactly one concurrent run, as expected

**Lint + Type check:**
No new lint or type errors introduced.

## Review
- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes
- Fixes #102238

target.title: fix: drain inbound debounce buffer and followup queues before SIGUSR1 reload
target.body:
## Problem

When `config.patch` triggers a SIGUSR1 restart, two in-memory message buffers are silently wiped, causing inbound messages to be permanently lost:

1. **Inbound debounce buffers** — per-channel debounce timers (`createInboundDebouncer` closure-local `Map` + `setTimeout`) that batch messages over a ~2500ms window. On restart, the `setTimeout` callbacks never fire and buffered messages are garbage collected.

2. **Followup queues** — the `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES` global `Map` that collects messages for sessions with active agent turns. Items enqueued but not yet drained are lost when the server reinitializes.

### Reproduction
Send a message on Signal → within 2.5s, trigger a config change (e.g. `config.patch`) → the message is silently dropped.

## Fix

### 1. Global debouncer registry (`src/auto-reply/inbound-debounce.ts`)
- Each `createInboundDebouncer()` now auto-registers in a shared `Symbol.for('openclaw.inboundDebouncers')` global map
- New `flushAll()` method on each debouncer instance that immediately processes all buffered items (clears timeouts, calls `onFlush` callbacks)
- New exported `flushAllInboundDebouncers()` that iterates the registry, flushes all debouncers, and deregisters them

### 2. Followup queue drain waiter (`src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain-all.ts`)
- New `waitForFollowupQueueDrain(timeoutMs)` that polls `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES` until all queues finish processing (or timeout)
- Counts `draining: true` queues as having pending work even if `items.length` is momentarily 0

### 3. SIGUSR1 restart integration (`src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts`)
Before `markGatewayDraining()`, the restart flow now:
1. `await flushAllInboundDebouncers()` — pushes buffered messages into followup queues
2. `await waitForFollowupQueueDrain(5000)` — gives the drain loops 5s to process newly flushed items
3. Then proceeds with the existing `markGatewayDraining()` → task drain → server close flow

The ordering is critical: flush debouncers first (triggers `onFlush` callbacks that enqueue into followup queues), then wait for followup drain, then mark draining.

## Tests

- **`src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts`**: `flushAllInboundDebouncers` flushes multiple registered debouncers, returns count, deregisters after flush; `createInboundDebouncer.flushAll` flushes all buffered keys
- **`src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain-all.test.ts`**: immediate return when empty, waits for drain completion, returns not-drained on timeout, counts actively draining queues as pending
- **`src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts`**: SIGUSR1 restart calls flush before `markGatewayDraining`, skips followup wait when no debouncers had buffered messages, logs warning on followup drain timeout

All 118 tests pass across the 4 affected test files. No type errors introduced.

## Files Changed
- `src/auto-reply/inbound-debounce.ts` — global registry + `flushAll` + `flushAllInboundDebouncers()`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain-all.ts` — new `waitForFollowupQueueDrain()`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/queue.ts` — barrel export
- `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts` — hook into restart flow
- Test files for all of the above

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: When a SIGUSR1 restart fires within the inbound debounce window (~2.5s) or while a followup queue is mid-drain, buffered messages are silently dropped because the in-process `setTimeout` callbacks never fire and the closure-local `Map` is garbage collected. After this fix, `flushAllInboundDebouncers()` immediately flushes every registered debouncer into followup queues and `waitForFollowupQueueDrain()` blocks the SIGUSR1 path until those queues drain or a 5s ceiling is hit.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at HEAD `5d1e6592d02782361b871581c10a6b3c0329105f` of branch `fix/drain-queue-before-sigusr1`. Linux 6.12.67, Node v24.15.0, pnpm-driven monorepo. Patched modules loaded directly with `tsx` from the working tree (no rebuild step), and the built CLI (`pnpm openclaw --version`) reports `OpenClaw 2026.5.4 (5d1e659)` confirming the binary is built from the patched commit.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. `pnpm openclaw --version` to confirm the live CLI is built from the patched HEAD.
  2. `node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-pr46303.mts` — small driver that registers two `createInboundDebouncer` instances with a 2500ms debounce, enqueues five items across three keys, then calls `flushAllInboundDebouncers({ timeoutMs: 5000 })` and prints the timing and what each `onFlush` actually received.
  3. `node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-pr46303-drain.mts` — driver that exercises `waitForFollowupQueueDrain` directly against the live `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES` `Map` for three cases: empty registry, busy queue that drains at ~120ms, and a queue that stays busy past the timeout.
  4. `pnpm test src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain-all.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts` — full targeted suites for all three changed files.
- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal capture from running the patched modules in this worktree.

  Live CLI build proves the binary contains the patched code:

  ```
  $ pnpm openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.5.4 (5d1e659)
  ```

  `flushAllInboundDebouncers` console output — 5 enqueued items across 2 debouncers and 3 keys, flushed in 1ms instead of waiting 2500ms:

  ```
  [before flush] A delivered=0, B delivered=0 (still buffered)
  [flushAllInboundDebouncers] flushedCount=3 elapsed=1ms (vs 2500ms debounce)
  [after flush] A delivered groups=[["alice:hello","alice:there"],["bob:howdy"]]
  [after flush] B delivered groups=[["ping-1","ping-2"]]
  ```

  `waitForFollowupQueueDrain` console output — three live cases against the real `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES` map, including the timeout path that returns `drained:false` with the right `remaining` count:

  ```
  [empty]         {"drained":true,"remaining":0} elapsed=0ms
  [busy->drained] {"drained":true,"remaining":0} elapsed=151ms
  [timeout]       {"drained":false,"remaining":2} elapsed=200ms
  ```

  Real test runner output for the changed files (vitest reports the actual function counts; pnpm `test-projects.mjs` shards by project):

  ```
  [test] starting test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  24 passed (24)
     Duration  2.21s
  [test] starting test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply.config.ts
   Test Files  2 passed (2)
        Tests  71 passed (71)
     Duration  4.05s
  [test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 11.96s
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: `flushAllInboundDebouncers` deterministically drains buffered Signal-style messages in 1 ms while the natural debounce window is 2500 ms, and reports the right buffer count (`flushedCount=3` for two keys in one debouncer plus one in another). `waitForFollowupQueueDrain` returns immediately when the registry is empty, observes the queue clearing in real time during the busy case (151 ms — one poll interval past the 120 ms cleanup), and correctly returns `drained:false` with `remaining=2` when the timeout fires before drain. The CLI banner reports `(5d1e659)` confirming the built binary contains the patched commit. With the SIGUSR1 hook in `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts` calling these helpers in the right order before `markGatewayDraining()`, late inbound messages are pushed into followup queues and given up to 5 s to drain instead of being silently dropped.
- **What was not tested**: An end-to-end real-Signal SIGUSR1 reproduction was not executed on this machine (no signal-cli account paired here); the production restart path is exercised through `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts`, but a live Signal → `config.patch` → restart roundtrip on real `signal-cli` was not run. Behavior under simultaneous restart-while-flushing on a hung `onFlush` (the registered handle is intentionally retained on flush failure for a future sweep) was not exercised live; that path is covered only by the unit tests in `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts`.

target.title: feat: add hosted feed envelope verifier
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/25

## What Problem This Solves

Starts the hosted feed trust-verification implementation series by adding the signed envelope verifier primitives that later feed refresh and source-profile PRs can consume.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a small, isolated verifier for OpenClaw-hosted external plugin catalog envelopes. It verifies Ed25519 signatures over stable base64url payload bytes, accepts PEM or raw base64url public keys, validates the payload type, and only parses the feed after a trusted signature verifies.

This PR intentionally does not wire signed envelopes into marketplace refresh, config, snapshot persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility. Those stay in follow-up PRs from the RFC trust series.

The Ed25519 PEM/raw-key verification helpers are shared with device identity code so the new feed verifier does not fork a second signature implementation.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes yet. This is a draft implementation foundation for future signed hosted feed verification.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Signed hosted feed envelopes can be verified against an explicit trusted Ed25519 key; payload bytes changed after signing are rejected before the feed is trusted; malformed raw signature arrays are capped before filtering or verification.

Real environment tested:
Windows checkout `C:\src\openclaw-feeds-trust-envelope-verifier-fix` at PR head `c6525aa6b7`; source harness using `node --import tsx -`; generated in-memory Ed25519 proof key; no network service or persisted cache involved. The clean worktree uses an ignored `node_modules` junction to the hydrated local OpenClaw checkout for tooling only.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Run a source harness that imports `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopePayload`, `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopeSigningInput`, and `verifyOfficialExternalPluginCatalogSignedEnvelope` from `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts`.
2. Generate an Ed25519 keypair, sign a minimal `clawhub-official` feed envelope, verify it with the trusted public key, then change the payload sequence and verify the original signature no longer validates.
3. Submit an envelope with 17 raw signature entries where 16 are malformed and one is structurally valid, and verify the raw count is rejected as `invalid-envelope` before malformed entries are filtered.

Evidence after fix:
```text
> node --import tsx -
envelope source harness passed: valid signed feed accepted; tampered payload rejected; excessive raw signatures rejected

target.title: refactor(qa): retire the standalone Matrix QA runtime
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix release QA had two independently maintained execution systems: the QA Lab scenario host and a standalone `qa-matrix` plugin with its own runtime, catalog, profiles, artifacts, retries, and workflow jobs. That second path let scenario coverage, credentials, lifecycle behavior, and release status drift depending on which runner was selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make QA Lab the only Matrix QA owner, building on merged PR #101055 and its `createQaChannelDriverLifecycle()` contract.

- Removes the `extensions/qa-matrix` package/plugin, registrations, dependencies, private runtime/catalog, Matrix-only artifacts, and standalone release orchestration.
- Keeps `pnpm openclaw qa matrix` only as a thin QA Lab selector for the shared scenario/profile host and selected Matrix transport adapter.
- Represents migrated Matrix behavior as ordinary QA Lab `kind: flow` scenarios. A compact `flow.module` / `flow.call` declaration becomes a shared QA Lab flow step; there is no Matrix fixture API or adapter-owned scenario runner.
- Uses the selected adapter only for lifecycle and flow preparation. `live:matrix` prepares the live Matrix scenario context and `crabline:matrix` remains selectable for portable flows through the same QA Lab execution path.
- Keeps scenario selection, sequencing, retries, timeouts, assertions, artifacts, and failure reporting in QA Lab instead of the transport adapter.
- Maps all 94 historical scenario IDs: 81 keep same-ID module-backed flows and 13 renamed IDs map to maintained QA Lab scenarios.

No compatibility fallback is retained because it would recreate a second Matrix execution path.

## User Impact

Maintainers and release managers get one Matrix QA implementation and evidence format.

- `qa matrix --profile release` remains the focused two-scenario release selector.
- `qa matrix --profile fast` retains 11 scenarios.
- `qa matrix --profile transport` retains 50 scenarios.
- Media and E2EE profiles retain their previous membership.
- `qa matrix` / `--profile all` retains the 92-scenario default profile, with two legacy explicit-only scenarios still excluded from the default exactly as before.
- Per-scenario provider mode, Matrix config, retry count, timeout, artifacts, and failure semantics are preserved.

There is no shipped Matrix channel runtime change. Packaged OpenClaw releases continue to omit private QA Lab tooling.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(stream): recover visible content when reasoning_delta straddles an inline code span (closes #96869)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a reasoning model emits a single streaming chunk carrying both `content` (visible) and `reasoning_content` deltas, and the model crosses modes mid-inline-code-span (the visible delta ends with an opener single backtick with no closer, and the reasoning delta carries the matching closer), the visible content is persisted with an **unclosed inline code span** and the matching half + everything after is silently routed into a private `thinking` block. Users see a reply truncated mid-sentence at a backtick; the remainder is hidden and never displayed.

Ref: #96869 (issue with full root-cause analysis and a runnable TS repro against upstream source).

## Root cause

In `src/llm/providers/openai-completions.ts` and `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts`, when a chunk carries both deltas, `appendPartitionedContent` routes the `content` delta through `reasoningTagTextPartitioner.push|pushVisible`, but `appendThinkingDelta` writes the `reasoning_content` delta **directly to the thinking block, bypassing the partitioner**. The partitioner never sees the closer backtick, so the visible block is finalized with an unclosed inline code span and the matching half is locked into a private thinking block.

The partitioner itself correctly tracks inline-code state across chunks (its existing tests cover cross-chunk code spans — see `preserves code-span reasoning tag examples when the closing backtick arrives later`). The bug is that `appendThinkingDelta` doesn't consult that state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Without this fix, any OpenAI-compatible reasoning provider that interleaves `content` and `reasoning_content` (Venice `claude-opus-4-8`, `zai-org-glm-5-2`, OpenAI o-series, qwen3-style servers, Anthropic-via-OpenAI proxies, etc.) can silently lose user-visible reply content. The failure is intermittent but message-loss-class.

## User Impact

- **Before:** reasoning-model replies could be persisted truncated mid-sentence at an unclosed backtick. The remainder lived in a `thinking` block in the session log and was never rendered to the user. No error was surfaced to operators or users.
- **After:** the partitioner is consulted before writing a reasoning delta to the thinking block. If the visible stream is mid-unclosed inline code span, the reasoning delta is routed as visible text and the open code span closes naturally. Existing reasoning flows (reasoningDepth > 0, or visible stream balanced) are byte-identical.

Provider-agnostic — fixes any reasoning provider routed through `openai-completions` or `openai-transport-stream`.

## Evidence

### Repro (before → after)

Running the exact failure scenario against the partitioner, simulating the routing order in `openai-completions.ts`:

```ts
const partitioner = createReasoningTagTextPartitioner();
const visible: string[] = [];
const thinking: string[] = [];

// One streaming chunk where the provider emits BOTH:
//   choice.delta.content         = "Visible. It uses a `"      // ends with opener backtick, no closer
//   choice.delta.reasoning_content = " blocks) and more"        // model crossed back to thinking mid-span
partitioner.markStrict();
for (const d of partitioner.push("Visible. It uses a `")) {
  (d.kind === "text" ? visible : thinking).push(d.text);
}
thinking.push(" blocks) and more"); // simulate appendThinkingDelta bypassing partitioner
for (const d of partitioner.flush()) {
  (d.kind === "text" ? visible : thinking).push(d.text);
}
```

- **Before this PR:** visible = `"Visible. It uses a \``" (1 backtick, unclosed), thinking = `" blocks) and more"` — content lost from visible.
- **After this PR:** visible = `"Visible. It uses a \` blocks) and more"` (2 backticks, balanced), no thinking block.

### Real-world failure (before)

Observed on OpenClaw 2026.6.9 (npm global), Venice `claude-opus-4-8` and `zai-org-glm-5-2`. Persisted assistant reply (501 chars, truncated at unclosed backtick):

> Got the full page now. Here's the honest read — and your "better than GLM" claim is *half* right in a way that actually makes it more interesting, not less.
>
> ## What Ornith-1.0-397B actually is
>
> - **397B MoE**, post-trained on Gemma 4 + Qwen 3.5
> - **MIT licensed** — fully open, no regional restrictions
> - **Built for agentic coding** — tool calling, terminal agents, SWE-bench. It's a reasoning model (`

The matching half was stored in a `thinking` block in the OpenClaw session, never displayed:

> ` blocks).
> - Notably: it explicitly lists **OpenClaw** and **OpenCode** as supported harnesses. This model is *built* for the exact kind of work we do.

### Tests added

- `src/shared/text/reasoning-tag-text-partitioner.test.ts` — 2 tests for the new `isInsideUnclosedVisibleInlineCode()` (unclosed across chunks, false while inside reasoning).
- `src/llm/providers/openai-completions.test.ts` — regression test for the exact chunk shape in the repro: content ending in opener backtick + reasoning-only chunk with the continuation. Asserts visible text `"Visible. It uses a \` blocks) and more"` with balanced backticks and **no** `thinking` block.

### Test results (local lane, on `origin/main` @ 95b97e5b0b)

- `pnpm test src/shared/text/reasoning-tag-text-partitioner.test.ts` → 28 / 28 pass (26 existing + 2 new)
- `pnpm test src/llm/providers/openai-completions.test.ts` → 32 / 32 pass (31 existing + 1 new regression)
- `pnpm test src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` → 266 pass / 10 fail — **the 10 failures are pre-existing on clean `main`** (verified by stashing this change: same 266 pass / 10 fail). All unrelated DeepSeek DSML / ModelStudio / Qwen / DashScope streaming-usage tests.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` → clean exit, no type errors.
- `pnpm build` (tsdown) → success; dist bundles contain the new `isInsideUnclosedVisibleInlineCode` symbol.

## AI-assisted

Yes — this PR was authored with AI assistance. The diagnosis, repro, fix, and tests were produced with an AI coding agent (Eva / OpenClaw). I (the human author) reviewed the diff and the test results.

## Checklist

- [x] Marked AI-assisted above
- [x] Evidence included (repro + real-world failure + test results)
- [x] Focused PR (one bug, one fix lane: 3 source files + 2 test files)
- [x] Existing partitioner + provider tests still pass
- [x] No CHANGELOG edits (per CONTRIBUTING)
- [x] No refactor-only or unrelated changes
- [x] Branch is on a fork; "Allow edits by maintainers" left enabled (default for fork PRs)
- [x] American English spelling in code/comments

Happy to revise per maintainer review. The two valid fix directions discussed in the issue were (a) route the `reasoning_content` delta through the partitioner as well, or (b) guard `appendThinkingDelta`. This PR implements (b) — the more surgical fix that preserves the partitioner's current behavior for genuine reasoning flows. If (a) is preferred, I can revise.

target.title: feat(context-engine): add reference context channel
target.body:
Closes #88753

## What Problem This Solves

Context-engine authors need a safe way to provide historical summaries, memories, or retrieved context without encoding that data as fresh current-user input or higher-authority prompt additions. Without a dedicated lane, compacted/reference data can regain too much prompt authority or interfere with provider message constraints.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow `AssembleResult.referenceContext` SDK lane plus a `reference-context` host capability. Native Codex app-server hosts now project that lane into Codex `turn/start.additionalContext` with `kind: "untrusted"`, so Codex owns the lower-authority external-fragment rendering instead of OpenClaw splicing the data into `turn/start.input`.

Embedded OpenClaw runs no longer advertise `reference-context`; they still support `assemble-before-prompt`, but engines that require a true reference-context lane are rejected there until embedded has an equivalent non-message transport.

## User Impact

Context-engine and plugin developers can return historical/reference data separately from executable model-history messages. Users get safer continuity because native Codex receives the reference data through its dedicated additional-context protocol lane while chat-only/current-user prompt text stays focused on the current request.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof from a redacted local OpenClaw `runCodexAppServerAttempt` test using a fake app-server client that captures the outgoing `turn/start` params:

```text
turn/start.input contains current request: true
turn/start.input contains OpenClaw reference context: false
turn/start.additionalContext.openclaw_reference_context.kind: untrusted
turn/start.additionalContext.openclaw_reference_context.value contains reference summary: true
```

Real Codex app-server proof using installed `@openai/codex` 0.142.4, `codex app-server --listen stdio://`, isolated `CODEX_HOME`, and a local mock `/v1/responses` server:

```text
responseRequestCount: 1
model request contains current prompt "inspect tab": true
model request contains external reference fragment: true
external fragment:
<external_openclaw_reference_context>OpenClaw reference context for this turn:
- Reference note: browser tab title is Example Domain.</external_openclaw_reference_context>

model input item summary:
- developer instructions item
- AGENTS/environment context item
- separate user item with <external_openclaw_reference_context>...</external_openclaw_reference_context>
- separate current user item: inspect tab
```

Additional real Codex app-server clear/replace proof with the same installed app-server and mock `/v1/responses` server:

```text
turn 1 additionalContext value: Reference A
turn 1 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn

turn 2 additionalContext value: Reference B
turn 2 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn, external Reference B, second turn

turn 3 additionalContext omitted
turn 3 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn, external Reference B, second turn, third turn no reference
thirdTurnHasNewExternalImmediatelyBeforePrompt: false
```

That matches Codex core behavior: `AdditionalContextStore::merge(values)` replaces the retained map with the current turn's map, and omitted app-server `additionalContext` maps to an empty map. Prior external fragments remain only as ordinary earlier transcript history; no fresh `openclaw_reference_context` fragment is injected before the current prompt when OpenClaw omits reference context.

Codex source contract checked locally in sibling `../codex`:

- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs` defines experimental `turn/start.additionalContext` as camelCase `additionalContext`.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs` maps omitted `additionalContext` to an empty core map.
- `codex-rs/core/src/state/additional_context.rs` replaces the retained additional-context map on each turn.
- `codex-rs/context-fragments/src/additional_context.rs` renders untrusted entries as `<external_{key}>...</external_{key}>` fragments.
- `codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/turn_start.rs` covers `turn_start_additional_context_flows_to_model_input`.
- `codex-rs/core/tests/suite/additional_context.rs` covers replacement/removal behavior and additional context being model-visible without becoming the current user turn item.

It makes each published container release produce inspectable SBOM artifacts, uploads Trivy vulnerability findings into GitHub Code Scanning, and gates the release only on fixed critical vulnerabilities. Generate SPDX and CycloneDX SBOM artifacts for released container images,

target.title: ACP: add gateway-owned node-backed runtime
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw did not yet have a complete **node-backed ACP runtime** where the gateway owns the durable state and a paired node acts only as the execution worker.
- Why it matters: without that split, restart/replay/reconnect behavior is too dependent on the live process, which makes lease fencing, terminal resolution, and outward delivery recovery harder to reason about and prove.
- What this PR adds:
  - a durable ACP gateway store for sessions, runs, accepted worker events, leases, terminal state, replay targets, and projector checkpoints
  - gateway ingestion of ACP worker events coming back from paired nodes
  - a real node-host ACP worker bridge and gateway/node command plumbing
  - a durable ACP reply projection/replay path so restart recovery can resume from gateway state instead of only from the live iterator
  - startup recovery for incomplete ACP node runs
  - restart/reconnect/cancel/close race hardening with focused restart/replay test coverage
  - architecture / protocol / verification docs for the new backend
- Landing-only follow-up: after rebasing onto current `main`, this PR also includes a few **test-only** isolation fixes in Feishu / Google / Google Chat extension tests that were needed to make the landing branch green. Those are not ACP runtime behavior changes.

## What changed by area

### 1) Durable ACP gateway state

New ACP store/state plumbing under `src/acp/store/**`:

- persists ACP sessions and runs
- persists accepted worker events
- tracks leases / lease epochs
- resolves canonical terminal state on the gateway
- stores replay targets and projector checkpoints separately from the runtime cursor

This is the foundation that lets the gateway stay authoritative even when execution happens on a paired node.

### 2) Gateway ↔ node ACP worker path

Main implementation areas:

- `src/gateway/**`
- `src/infra/node-commands.ts`
- `src/node-host/**`

This adds the node-backed ACP execution path:

- gateway can start/control ACP work on a paired node
- node-host can run the ACP worker role
- worker events stream back to the gateway over the existing node transport
- gateway remains the source of truth for run state and terminal resolution

### 3) Durable reply projection and replay

Main implementation areas:

- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-replay.ts`

This PR moves ACP outward delivery onto a durable replayable path:

- reply targets are persisted per run
- projector checkpoints are advanced only after successful delivery
- restart recovery can replay the unfinished suffix from durable state
- reconnect and duplicate accepted events do not re-deliver already completed outward effects

### 4) Startup recovery / reconnect handling

Main implementation areas:

- `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-node-events.ts`
- `src/acp/runtime/acp-node.ts`

This adds the gateway-side recovery flow needed to:

- resume incomplete projection after restart
- keep reconnect handling deterministic
- prevent stale-worker wins
- preserve canonical terminal behavior across restart/replay windows

### 5) Test harnesses and regression coverage

Main test additions/expansions:

- `src/acp/store/store.restart.test.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.replay.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-node-events.acp.test.ts`
- `src/node-host/invoke-acp.test.ts`
- `src/acp/test-harness/restart-harness.ts`

These cover the core failure windows this backend needs to survive:

- restart after accepted events but before replay checkpoint advancement
- restart after terminal persistence but before final outward convergence
- reconnect replay of already accepted events
- cancel / complete / close race handling
- restart recovery with a real memory cut instead of reusing in-process objects

### 6) Docs included in this PR

Main docs:

- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime-protocol.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime-verification.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-runtime-program.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-slice4-summary.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-slice4-final-judge.md`

These are included because this was developed as a staged architecture / verification effort and the final accepted behavior is documented there.

## Explicit scope boundaries / v1 limitations

This PR does **not**:

- turn nodes into mini-gateways
- add automatic cross-node continuation for an in-flight run
- claim durable resumed tool-message edit support after restart

Current conservative post-restart tool-update behavior remains:

- `append_only_after_restart`

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [x] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related: ACP node runtime architecture / protocol / verification docs under `docs/experiments/plans/`
- Related: landing-only extension test isolation fixes after rebase onto current `main`

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- OpenClaw now has a first-class ACP node-backed runtime path where the gateway owns durable ACP truth and paired nodes execute the worker role.
- Gateway restart/recovery can resume incomplete ACP outward projection from durable state.
- Duplicate accepted worker-event replay on reconnect is hardened so it does not duplicate outward delivery.
- Post-restart tool updates intentionally follow the documented conservative v1 rule: `append_only_after_restart`.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? Yes
- Command/tool execution surface changed? Yes
- Data access scope changed? Yes

### Security / trust-boundary notes

- Paired nodes can now advertise ACP worker capability and receive ACP runtime commands over the existing gateway↔node trust boundary.
- Gateway↔node websocket traffic now carries ACP worker control / event flows in addition to existing node commands.
- Gateway now persists ACP runtime state needed for durable replay/recovery.
- The design mitigates stale-worker / duplicate-delivery risks via lease epochs, canonical terminal resolution, durable replay checkpoints, and reconnect/replay handling on the gateway.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux (landing worktree on vm1) + GitHub Actions CI
- Runtime/container: Node / pnpm; Bun build path also checked
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): ACP gateway↔node runtime path
- Relevant config (redacted): ACP runtime restart/replay harnesses and paired-node fixtures

### Verified locally

- ACP targeted verification gate:
  - `pnpm test -- src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.replay.test.ts src/acp/store/store.test.ts src/acp/store/store.restart.test.ts src/acp/store/gateway-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-node-events.acp.test.ts src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-acp.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.acp.test.ts`
- TypeScript guardrail:
  - `pnpm tsgo`
- Landing-only extension test fixes:
  - `pnpm test:extensions`

### CI / build notes

- `pnpm build` still fails only with the pre-existing Bun wrapper issue:
  - `Cannot find module './cjs/index.cjs' from ''`
- That build failure was already present and is not introduced by the ACP runtime changes in this PR.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What I personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified the ACP-focused local gate listed above.
- Verified `pnpm tsgo` passes.
- Verified the rebased landing branch’s extension test-isolation fixes with local `pnpm test:extensions`.
- Verified the PR now includes the architecture / protocol / verification / final-judge docs for this backend.

What I did **not** verify:

- I did **not** get a clean `pnpm build` because of the pre-existing Bun wrapper failure noted above.
- I did **not** run a fresh manual end-to-end Discord/real-node interactive repro outside the checked-in restart/replay and node-host harnesses.

## Review Guide

If you want the shortest path through this PR, review in this order:

1. **Core architecture / intent**
   - `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime.md`
   - `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime-protocol.md`
2. **Gateway-owned durable state**
   - `src/acp/store/**`
3. **Node execution bridge**
   - `src/node-host/**`
   - `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts`
   - `src/gateway/server-node-events.ts`
4. **Durable outward replay path**
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts`
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-replay.ts`
5. **Recovery and proofs**
   - `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.ts`
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.replay.test.ts`
   - `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.test.ts`
6. **Ignore as landing-only test fixes unless you are checking CI fallout**
   - `extensions/feishu/**`
   - `extensions/google/**`
   - `extensions/googlechat/**`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No explicit migration required
- Migration needed? No

Notes:

- This adds a new ACP runtime/backend path; it does not force existing deployments to switch to it immediately.
- Post-restart tool updates intentionally remain append-only in v1.

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert this PR or avoid selecting/using the `acp-node` runtime path until fixed.
- Files/config to restore: ACP runtime/store/gateway/node-host changes under `src/acp/**`, `src/node-host/**`, `src/gateway/**`, plus the accompanying docs if reverting wholesale.
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: duplicate final delivery after restart, stale worker winning after reconnect, projector checkpoint drift, or replay targeting the wrong route.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: restart/replay correctness is subtle in any durable projection system.
  - Mitigation: this PR includes restart harnesses, startup recovery tests, reconnect/replay ordering tests, and explicit protocol/verification docs.
- Risk: the PR is large and spans multiple ACP runtime layers.
  - Mitigation: the review guide above splits it into durable store, node bridge, replay path, recovery path, and landing-only CI fixes.
- Risk: paired-node ACP execution expands the gateway↔node command surface.
  - Mitigation: the gateway remains authoritative for leases, terminal resolution, checkpoints, and replay instead of trusting node-local completion.

---

## AI Checklist

- [x] **AI-assisted** — agent-harness / Codex driven implementation, review, and landing follow-ups
- [x] **Testing degree** — focused local verification plus CI
- [x] **Understanding confirmed** — this PR adds the gateway-owned ACP node-backed runtime and includes a few landing-only extension test fixes after rebase

target.title: feat(signal): add setup wizard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal setup needs a guided path that proves a usable receive transport before users rely on the channel, without OpenClaw creating or managing a Signal Docker container. The prior setup surface could also leave stale transport settings in config, report ambiguous probe state, or persist partial setup results after a failed/cancelled setup attempt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal setup now stays owned by the Signal plugin: users can configure a local `signal-cli` native daemon or connect OpenClaw to an existing Signal server they manage. Core setup only gains the generic `setupApplied: false` rollback signal needed to avoid selection hooks, callbacks, completion notes, and config persistence for unsuccessful setup attempts. Existing/manual `bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api` servers remain supported through `apiMode: "container"` and receive-readiness probes, but the wizard no longer offers an OpenClaw-managed Docker container path.

## User Impact

Users get Signal setup prompts for native `signal-cli` or an existing server URL, with account-aware receive probing before setup is accepted. Operators get clearer `channels status --probe` output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states. Multi-account Signal configs can scope `apiMode` per account while preserving channel-level `channels.signal.apiMode` as the default.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Existing-server setup prompts for the Signal phone number, probes the provided server with that account, and saves `httpUrl`, `autoStart: false`, and `apiMode: "auto"` only after the probe succeeds.
- Native setup clears stale external/container transport fields and saves native daemon settings for the intended account.
- Existing/manual container servers still validate `/v1/accounts` with bounded reads and require `/v1/receive/{account}` WebSocket readiness when receive capability is required.
- Failed or cancelled setup can return `setupApplied: false`, so core setup rolls back partial config and skips account-selection side effects.
- Approval reaction hints are only appended when a configured Signal account id exists, avoiding hints that cannot be registered for explicit `baseUrl` plus `account` sends.
- Screenshots are omitted because this PR changes terminal/setup wizard, gateway status, config, and docs behavior; command/test output is the reviewer-checkable proof.

Automated and review checks on head `824dcb55bf3b5236e6b49c3cee2084cb662aaae4`:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/setup-core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/send.test.ts extensions/signal/src/send-reactions.test.ts extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts` passed: 5 files, 180 tests.

target.title: feat: add user-specific memory isolation
target.body:
## Summary

Adds user-specific memory isolation to OpenClaw, enabling per-user memory files in multi-user environments.

## Changes

### Core Feature
- **MemoryIsolationConfig** type added to `src/config/types.memory.ts`
  - `isolation.enabled` (default: `true`) to enable/disable isolation

### Session Key Extraction
- **extractUserIdFromSessionKey()** added to `src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts`
  - Extracts userId from direct message session keys
  - Returns `null` for channel/group sessions

### Memory Path Access Control
- **isMemoryPath()** updated in `src/memory/internal.ts`
  - When `userId` is provided, enforces access control
  - Users can only access their own `memory/{userId}/` directory
  - Shared memory files at `memory/` root are accessible to all

### Memory Tools
- **memory_search** and **memory_get** tools updated
  - Accept optional `senderId` parameter
  - Falls back to `senderId` from inbound context when session key doesn't contain userId

### Plugin Integration
- **extensions/memory-core/index.ts** updated
  - Passes `requesterSenderId` from plugin context to memory tools

## How It Works

```
Session Type       | userId Source          | Memory Path
-------------------|------------------------|---------------------------
Direct Message     | sessionKey extraction  | memory/{userId}/YYYY-MM-DD.md
Channel/Group     | requesterSenderId      | memory/{senderId}/YYYY-MM-DD.md
Disabled (legacy)  | none                   | memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md (shared)
```

## Security

- Users cannot access other users' memory directories
- Path validation in `isMemoryPath()` prevents directory traversal
- Shared memory at `memory/` root is accessible to all (for global context)

## Testing

- Unit tests added in `src/memory/internal.test.ts`
- All existing tests pass

## Breaking Changes

None. The feature is opt-in via configuration and defaults to the new isolated behavior when `memory.isolation.enabled` is not set (defaults to `true`).

Users who want the old shared behavior can set:
```json
{
  "memory": {
    "isolation": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw had no built-in isolated rescue watchdog that could detect an unhealthy managed gateway profile and repair it without going through the failing primary session.

- What changed: adds daemon/service hardening needed by the watchdog, introduces a new isolated `rescueWatchdog` cron payload + runner, and wires the gateway cron service to execute that watchdog job against a monitored profile.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no onboarding wizard flow, no CLI `openclaw onboard --rescue-watchdog` UX, and no docs changes in this PR.

Risk is bounded by restricting the payload shape, disallowing delivery targets for `rescueWatchdog`, resolving the monitored profile explicitly, and hardening the underlying managed-service restart and launchd plist write paths. The repair fallback uses exact argv via `process.execPath` and avoids shell-based PATH resolution.

target.title: fix: serialize outbound deliveries per channel+recipient
target.body:
## Summary

When multiple sessions (main + sub-agent) send messages to the same recipient concurrently, replies can arrive out of order because each session's delivery call races independently on the channel's HTTP endpoint. Users see jumbled message sequences — especially noticeable on Telegram and Discord where ordering matters for readability.

**Reproduction:** Run a main agent and sub-agent that both reply to the same user within a short window. Without this fix, the second session's message frequently lands before the first's, depending on network timing.

**Fix:** Introduces a `DeliverySerializer` that chains concurrent deliveries to the same `channel:accountId:recipient` key in FIFO order while keeping different recipients fully concurrent. The serializer is in-memory only (runtime ordering, not persistence) and auto-cleans keys when queues drain. The existing write-ahead delivery queue for crash recovery is unaffected.

A follow-up commit wraps `fn()` in `Promise.resolve().then()` so a synchronous throw is converted to a rejection rather than hanging the result promise forever (addresses review feedback).

Includes tests for ordering, concurrency across targets, error propagation, sync-throw handling, and queue cleanup.

Rebased to 2026.3.13.

---

## Real behavior proof — Telegram, live session (2026-05-22)

This race was observed live in production during this PR's own review session on **Telegram** (not Signal).

**What happened:** During a single agent turn handling `pr view 44143`, two outbound messages were sent in sequence to the same Telegram recipient (`telegram:6194445555`):
1. A long ClawSweeper analysis dump (~4KB)
2. A summary message referencing and synthesizing that analysis

**Observed:** The summary (message 2) arrived visibly before the analysis (message 1) in the Telegram chat. The recipient had to read the synthesis before the content it was synthesizing — the exact inversion this PR fixes.

**Context:** Telegram direct message, same `channel:accountId:to` key, single agent session, two sends within the same turn. No sub-agent involved — the race can happen within a single session turn when one send is large enough to lose the HTTP timing race against a smaller follow-up send.

**Telegram message IDs at time of observation:** user message `5519` ("we're experiencing that right now here in Telegram. Look at your last 3 messages"), preceded by the two inverted agent messages. Timestamp: 2026-05-22 ~15:00 EDT.

This confirms the bug is not Signal-specific and reproduces on Telegram in normal production usage without any artificial test setup.

target.title: fix(skills): list omitted skill names when prompt is truncated
target.body:
## Problem

When many skills are installed (e.g. 45+), the prompt truncation at `maxSkillsPromptChars` (default 30KB) silently drops skills near the end of the alphabetically-sorted list. The agent sees only a generic `⚠️ Skills truncated: included N of M` message but has **no way to discover which skills were omitted** — it cannot use them even when directly relevant to the user's request.

Real-world example: a user sends a `mp.weixin.qq.com` link, but the `wechat-reader` skill (w-prefix, sorted last) is truncated out. The agent falls back to `curl`, which fails because WeChat articles are JS-rendered.

## Solution

When skills are truncated, the note now includes the **names** of omitted skills (capped at 1KB to stay compact) and suggests `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` so the agent can still discover and read them on demand.

**Before:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit.
```

**After:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit. Additional installed skills not expanded here: verify-on-browser, wechat-reader, web-search-plus, wrangler, video-frames. If a listed skill name becomes relevant, inspect it with `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` before deciding whether to read its SKILL.md.
```

## Changes

- `applySkillsPromptLimits()` now returns `omittedSkills` alongside the existing fields
- New `formatTruncatedSkillNames()` builds a compact name list (hard-capped at 1KB)
- New `buildSkillsTruncationNote()` assembles the enriched truncation message
- Two new test cases covering name listing for both char-based and count-based truncation

## Tests

All 34 existing + new tests pass (`npx vitest run src/agents/skills`).

## Real behavior proof

target.title: feat(github-copilot): support GitHub Enterprise data-residency Copilot auth
target.body:
> **AI-assisted PR.** Implemented with the GitHub Copilot CLI (Claude). The author has reviewed and understands all changes; validated locally (targeted Vitest suites, `tsgo` typecheck, oxlint/oxfmt, SDK surface budget) and against a live `*.ghe.com` tenant (see Evidence). ## What Problem This Solves Organizations on a data-residency GitHub Enterprise tenant (a `*.ghe.com` host such as `your-org.ghe.com`) could not use GitHub Copilot with OpenClaw. Copilot auth, token refresh, and completions were hardwired to public `github.com` / `api.github.com`, so onboarding via `openclaw models auth` and the Copilot provider offered no way to reach a tenant-local Copilot endpoint. Enterprise users were effectively locked out of the Copilot provider. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds GitHub Enterprise (data residency) as a first-class Copilot auth choice, nested alongside the existing GitHub and Local Proxy options. Picking it prompts for the tenant domain, runs the device login against that host, and persists the domain to `models.providers.github-copilot.params.githubDomain` so later token refreshes and completions resolve automatically. Domain resolution follows `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` env > config > `github.com`. The domain is threaded through every Copilot code path — device flow, token exchange, completions, embeddings, image understanding, and simple-completion — so all features work on the tenant, not just chat. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged (no config is written for the default host). No config schema change (uses free-form provider params). **Security (fail-closed by design):** the host allowlist is locked to `github.com` and `*.ghe.com` tenants only — any other value (typo or injected `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN`/config) falls back to `github.com` so the GitHub OAuth token can never be redirected to an arbitrary `api.`. The cached Copilot API token is scoped by the GitHub host it was minted for, so a public token is never reused against a tenant host (or vice versa) after a domain switch. **Domain-switch re-authentication:** onboarding no longer reuses a stored Copilot token when the selected domain differs from the one the token was minted under. Any switch (public `github.com` ↔ a `*.ghe.com` tenant, or one tenant to another) forces a fresh device login so the persisted `githubDomain` always matches a tenant-scoped token; re-running login for the *same* domain still offers to reuse the current token. Switching back to public `github.com` clears the persisted `githubDomain` so config returns to the default (no config == `github.com`). This closes the gap where declining re-login could write a tenant domain against an unverified public token. ## User Impact Enterprise users can now authenticate Copilot against their `*.ghe.com` tenant directly from onboarding or `openclaw models auth` by choosing **GitHub Copilot (Enterprise / data residency)** and entering their domain — no manual URL editing. Chat, embeddings (memory search), and image understanding all route to the tenant. `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` enables fully headless/CI setups. Non-enterprise users see no change. ## Scope & Related Work Closes #102219. This PR extends the **existing bundled `github-copilot` provider** with data-residency domain support for the auth, token-exchange, and completions paths it already ships. It does **not** add a new provider, a new model catalog, or a config-schema change (it uses free-form provider params). Related: #96988 ("GHE.com Model Integration"), which was closed NOT_PLANNED and routed to ClawHub/plugin scope. That issue asked for a broader/new GHE model integration; this change is deliberately narrower: it makes the provider OpenClaw already bundles honor an allowlisted, fail-closed `*.ghe.com` tenant host so enterprise users are not locked out, without introducing new SDK provider surface. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged. **AI-assisted:** developed and validated with AI coding agents (Copilot, Claude) under human direction; all changes human-reviewed, with live tenant validation run by the author. ## Evidence Live validation against a real data-residency GHE tenant (domain/token redacted): ### [P1] GHE Login, Token Refresh & Completion — Redacted Evidence 1. GHE Login / Auth pre-warm (gateway startup, 18:56:23 UTC) ``` subsystem=gateway level=INFO time=2026-07-02T18:56:23.756Z provider auth state pre-warmed in 477ms eventLoopMax=11.9ms ``` Stored GHE credential loaded and validated successfully on gateway boot. 2. Active GHE Copilot token state ``` integrationId: vscode-chat token: [REDACTED] updatedAt: 2026-07-02T21:03:31Z ← refreshed ~12 minutes ago expiresAt: 2026-07-02T21:33:31Z ← valid for ~17 more minutes expired? false ``` Standard 30-minute Copilot token TTL confirmed; token was refreshed mid-session against REDACTED.ghe.com. 3. Completion calls against GHE endpoint (sample) ``` subsystem=provider-transport-fetch level=INFO time=2026-07-02T21:09:19Z [model-fetch] start provider=github-copilot api=anthropic-messages model=claude-sonnet-4.6 method=POST url=https://copilot-api.REDACTED.ghe.com/v1/messages status=— [model-fetch] response provider=github-copilot api=anthropic-messages model=claude-sonnet-4.6 status=200 elapsedMs=1529 contentType=text/event-stream ``` Dozens of successful round-trips throughout the session (18:56 → 21:15 UTC), all status=200.

target.title: fix(stream): recover visible content when reasoning_delta straddles an inline code span (closes #96869)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a reasoning model emits a single streaming chunk carrying both `content` (visible) and `reasoning_content` deltas, and the model crosses modes mid-inline-code-span (the visible delta ends with an opener single backtick with no closer, and the reasoning delta carries the matching closer), the visible content is persisted with an **unclosed inline code span** and the matching half + everything after is silently routed into a private `thinking` block. Users see a reply truncated mid-sentence at a backtick; the remainder is hidden and never displayed.

Ref: #96869 (issue with full root-cause analysis and a runnable TS repro against upstream source).

## Root cause

In `src/llm/providers/openai-completions.ts` and `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts`, when a chunk carries both deltas, `appendPartitionedContent` routes the `content` delta through `reasoningTagTextPartitioner.push|pushVisible`, but `appendThinkingDelta` writes the `reasoning_content` delta **directly to the thinking block, bypassing the partitioner**. The partitioner never sees the closer backtick, so the visible block is finalized with an unclosed inline code span and the matching half is locked into a private thinking block.

The partitioner itself correctly tracks inline-code state across chunks (its existing tests cover cross-chunk code spans — see `preserves code-span reasoning tag examples when the closing backtick arrives later`). The bug is that `appendThinkingDelta` doesn't consult that state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Without this fix, any OpenAI-compatible reasoning provider that interleaves `content` and `reasoning_content` (Venice `claude-opus-4-8`, `zai-org-glm-5-2`, OpenAI o-series, qwen3-style servers, Anthropic-via-OpenAI proxies, etc.) can silently lose user-visible reply content. The failure is intermittent but message-loss-class.

## User Impact

- **Before:** reasoning-model replies could be persisted truncated mid-sentence at an unclosed backtick. The remainder lived in a `thinking` block in the session log and was never rendered to the user. No error was surfaced to operators or users.
- **After:** the partitioner is consulted before writing a reasoning delta to the thinking block. If the visible stream is mid-unclosed inline code span, the reasoning delta is routed as visible text and the open code span closes naturally. Existing reasoning flows (reasoningDepth > 0, or visible stream balanced) are byte-identical.

Provider-agnostic — fixes any reasoning provider routed through `openai-completions` or `openai-transport-stream`.

## Evidence

### Repro (before → after)

Running the exact failure scenario against the partitioner, simulating the routing order in `openai-completions.ts`:

```ts
const partitioner = createReasoningTagTextPartitioner();
const visible: string[] = [];
const thinking: string[] = [];

// One streaming chunk where the provider emits BOTH:
//   choice.delta.content         = "Visible. It uses a `"      // ends with opener backtick, no closer
//   choice.delta.reasoning_content = " blocks) and more"        // model crossed back to thinking mid-span
partitioner.markStrict();
for (const d of partitioner.push("Visible. It uses a `")) {
  (d.kind === "text" ? visible : thinking).push(d.text);
}
thinking.push(" blocks) and more"); // simulate appendThinkingDelta bypassing partitioner
for (const d of partitioner.flush()) {
  (d.kind === "text" ? visible : thinking).push(d.text);
}
```

- **Before this PR:** visible = `"Visible. It uses a \``" (1 backtick, unclosed), thinking = `" blocks) and more"` — content lost from visible.
- **After this PR:** visible = `"Visible. It uses a \` blocks) and more"` (2 backticks, balanced), no thinking block.

### Real-world failure (before)

Observed on OpenClaw 2026.6.9 (npm global), Venice `claude-opus-4-8` and `zai-org-glm-5-2`. Persisted assistant reply (501 chars, truncated at unclosed backtick):

> Got the full page now. Here's the honest read — and your "better than GLM" claim is *half* right in a way that actually makes it more interesting, not less.
>
> ## What Ornith-1.0-397B actually is
>
> - **397B MoE**, post-trained on Gemma 4 + Qwen 3.5
> - **MIT licensed** — fully open, no regional restrictions
> - **Built for agentic coding** — tool calling, terminal agents, SWE-bench. It's a reasoning model (`

The matching half was stored in a `thinking` block in the OpenClaw session, never displayed:

> ` blocks).
> - Notably: it explicitly lists **OpenClaw** and **OpenCode** as supported harnesses. This model is *built* for the exact kind of work we do.

### Tests added

- `src/shared/text/reasoning-tag-text-partitioner.test.ts` — 2 tests for the new `isInsideUnclosedVisibleInlineCode()` (unclosed across chunks, false while inside reasoning).
- `src/llm/providers/openai-completions.test.ts` — regression test for the exact chunk shape in the repro: content ending in opener backtick + reasoning-only chunk with the continuation. Asserts visible text `"Visible. It uses a \` blocks) and more"` with balanced backticks and **no** `thinking` block.

### Test results (local lane, on `origin/main` @ 95b97e5b0b)

- `pnpm test src/shared/text/reasoning-tag-text-partitioner.test.ts` → 28 / 28 pass (26 existing + 2 new)
- `pnpm test src/llm/providers/openai-completions.test.ts` → 32 / 32 pass (31 existing + 1 new regression)
- `pnpm test src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` → 266 pass / 10 fail — **the 10 failures are pre-existing on clean `main`** (verified by stashing this change: same 266 pass / 10 fail). All unrelated DeepSeek DSML / ModelStudio / Qwen / DashScope streaming-usage tests.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` → clean exit, no type errors.
- `pnpm build` (tsdown) → success; dist bundles contain the new `isInsideUnclosedVisibleInlineCode` symbol.

## AI-assisted

Yes — this PR was authored with AI assistance. The diagnosis, repro, fix, and tests were produced with an AI coding agent (Eva / OpenClaw). I (the human author) reviewed the diff and the test results.

## Checklist

- [x] Marked AI-assisted above
- [x] Evidence included (repro + real-world failure + test results)
- [x] Focused PR (one bug, one fix lane: 3 source files + 2 test files)
- [x] Existing partitioner + provider tests still pass
- [x] No CHANGELOG edits (per CONTRIBUTING)
- [x] No refactor-only or unrelated changes
- [x] Branch is on a fork; "Allow edits by maintainers" left enabled (default for fork PRs)
- [x] American English spelling in code/comments

Happy to revise per maintainer review. The two valid fix directions discussed in the issue were (a) route the `reasoning_content` delta through the partitioner as well, or (b) guard `appendThinkingDelta`. This PR implements (b) — the more surgical fix that preserves the partitioner's current behavior for genuine reasoning flows. If (a) is preferred, I can revise.
